nodes.description: Biallelic FOXE1 variants disrupt the function of the forkhead/winged-helix transcription factor TTF-2. Most reported forkhead-domain mutations impair DNA binding and transcriptional activity; FOXE1 is expressed in the developing thyroid, foregut endoderm and craniopharyngeal ectoderm, so its dysfunction is the shared initiating lesion across the thyroid and craniofacial features of the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: The mutant protein exhibits impaired DNA binding and loss of transcriptional function.

evidence.snippet: TTF-2 is a member of the forkhead/winged-helix domain transcription factor family, many of which are key regulators of embryogenesis.

nodes.description: A sequela of congenital hypothyroidism when thyroid hormone replacement is not started early; it is preventable with timely treatment rather than an invariant feature.

nodes.description: FOXE1 is a Shh/Gli target expressed in the hair follicle; loss of FOXE1 function disrupts hair follicle morphogenesis and orientation, producing the abnormal (spiky) hair.

evidence.reference_title: Requirement of the forkhead gene Foxe1, a target of sonic hedgehog signaling, in hair follicle morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Foxe1-null skin displays aberrant hair formation with the production of thinner and curly pelage hairs.

evidence.reference_title: Requirement of the forkhead gene Foxe1, a target of sonic hedgehog signaling, in hair follicle morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Our findings provide a strong indication that the defect in Bamforth-Lazarus syndrome is due to altered FOXE1 function in the hair follicle

nodes.description: FOXE1 directly regulates MSX1 and TGF-beta3, which are required for secondary palate fusion. Loss of FOXE1 function reduces palatal MSX1 and TGF-beta3 expression and prevents palatal shelf fusion, causing cleft palate.

evidence.reference_title: MSX1 and TGF-beta3 are novel target genes functionally regulated by FOXE1.
evidence.snippet: In 14-day Foxe1(-/-) mice embryos, Tgf-β3 and Msx1 mRNAs were almost absent in palatal shelves compared with Foxe1(+/-) embryos.

evidence.reference_title: MSX1 and TGF-beta3 are novel target genes functionally regulated by FOXE1.
evidence.snippet: MSX1 and TGF-β3 are direct FOXE1 targets.

nodes.description: FOXE1 drives thyroid gland morphogenesis; its expression in thyroid precursors is down-regulated as they cease migration. Loss of FOXE1 function arrests thyroid development, producing thyroid agenesis (athyreosis) or a sublingual/hypoplastic gland.

evidence.reference_title: A mouse model for hereditary thyroid dysgenesis and cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: Expression of Titf2 in thyroid cell precursors is down-regulated as they cease migration, suggesting that this factor is involved in the process of thyroid gland morphogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: A mouse model for hereditary thyroid dysgenesis and cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: Titf2-null mutant mice exhibit cleft palate and either a sublingual or completely absent thyroid gland.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in human TTF-2 (FKHL15) gene associated with congenital hypothyroidism but not athyreosis.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that human thyroid development can occur despite loss of TTF-2 function and suggest that TTF-2 gene defects should also be considered in cases of syndromic CH without total athyreosis.

nodes.description: With the thyroid gland absent or severely hypoplastic, thyroid hormone cannot be synthesised, producing congenital hypothyroidism. Here the disorder-specific lesion substituted into the conserved hypothyroidism pathway is thyroid agenesis rather than dyshormonogenesis or autoimmune destruction.

evidence.snippet: this mutant gene enhanced the activity of the TG and TPO gene promoters (1.5-fold and 1.7-fold respectively vs. wild type FOXE1; p<0.05), unlike the five mutations previously reported in Bamforth-Lazarus syndrome.
